title: What does a Digital ID mean to a refugee’s self-identity?
html:
That is almost the exact question Zoey Zhang asked me when we had our first call at the beginning of 2022. When I was put in touch with Zoey, I had never heard or thought of a dedicated degree in digital sociology. But, with a couple minutes of reflection, it became obvious that such studies should exist given the direction of our (digital) world.

Zoey joined me a couple months later and started the task of trying to answer the question within the humanitarian sector. It was easy to find people outlining all the benefits that a Digital ID would have for responding agencies (e.g. efficiencies, remove duplication, eliminate fraud, etc.). It was also easy to find feel-good stories about Digital ID successes (e.g. refugees in Cameroon - PDF). But it seemed that very few people had pondered how issuing Digital IDs may affect those affected by disaster. Does it change how people think of themselves? Does it change how they present themselves to others? Does it introduce more have and have-nots when technology is required?

It has been an exciting journey to work with Zoey and learn more about identification than I had ever thought about before. And, to really think of such topics from a sociological perspective rather than that of a responding agency trying to improve our approach.

Today, we are excited to share the final report: The Humanitarian Sector & Digital Identity: Are We Affecting Refugee’s Self-Identities?

[PDF]

In terms of what we found, throughout our research, no strong relationship between digital identity in the refugee context and one’s (self) “identity” was recognized. Therefore, we could not draw a decisive conclusion that digital identity does or does not have influence on an affected person’s identity. It varies by context, circumstance and person. And since our interviewees were all responders rather than affected people, our information and understanding are largely third-hand. Clearly there is room for more research on the topic especially if one can engage Digital ID recipients directly. 

Andrej
teaser: Research with Zoey Zhang on how Digital ID may change how refugees see themselves, based on interviews with responders rather than affected people.
seo_description: Zoey Zhang and Andrej Verity examine the effects of Digital ID on refugees' self-identity, noting that interviewees were responders and more research is needed.
